match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the circle theorem that the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc; the closest, on triangle angle facts, covers a different idea.

draft.title: Angle at the centre and the circumference
card: An arc is part of a circle's edge. An angle at the centre has its vertex at the centre of the circle. An angle at the circumference has its vertex on the edge.
Both angles can stand on the same arc, which means their arms meet the circle at the same two end points of the arc.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc. So the angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre.
The angle at the centre is \(80^{\circ}\). The angle at the circumference on the same arc is \(80^{\circ} \div 2 = 40^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Centre angle \(= 2 \times\) circumference angle, on the same arc.

a.q: An angle at the centre of a circle is \(110^{\circ}\). What is the angle at the circumference on the same arc?
a.why: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre, so \(110^{\circ} \div 2 = 55^{\circ}\). Doubling to get \(220^{\circ}\) reverses the rule, because the centre angle is the larger one.
a.clue: Which angle is larger, the one at the centre or the one at the edge?

b.q: Points A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. The angle ACB at the circumference is \(34^{\circ}\) and stands on arc AB. What is the angle AOB at the centre on the same arc?
b.why: Both angles stand on arc AB, so the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference: \(2 \times 34^{\circ} = 68^{\circ}\). Halving to get \(17^{\circ}\) is tempting, but the unknown angle is the one at the centre, so it is the larger.
b.clue: You are finding the centre angle, so it should be the bigger one.

wants.brief: A circle with centre O and points A and B on the circumference. Point C lies on the major arc. Draw the angle AOB at the centre, labelled 80 degrees, and the angle ACB at the circumference standing on the same arc AB, labelled 40 degrees. Label the arc AB.
wants.why: Seeing both angles stand on the same arc shows which angle is at the centre and which is at the circumference.
